CurrentLocation: In situ, Tel Dan Nature Reserve
Description: The great raised platform and altar court at Dan, excavated by Avraham Biran, where Jeroboam set one of his golden calves and told Israel it was too much to go up to Jerusalem. This entry covers the high place structure only; the Tel Dan Stele, an inscription found at the same site, has its own entry.
BiblicalSignificance: Dan is where convenience became idolatry. A king who feared losing his people built them a nearer god, and the platform he raised still stands as a warning: worship shaped by politics, however grand its stones, is not worship of the LORD.
Interpretations: Scholars broadly accept the platform as the high place of 1 Kings 12; the precise phasing of its construction across the 10th–8th centuries is debated.
